output.explanation: If a site's status is exactly "ACTIVE", it must have an activated_on value that is present and not an empty string. Sites with any other status always pass, whatever activated_on holds.
fails_when: status is "ACTIVE" and activated_on is null
The status comparison is case-sensitive, so "active" is not treated as ACTIVE and passes without any check on activated_on

Surprising: activated_on is a date (NAIVE_DATE) but is compared to the empty string "". That second check can never be false for a real date, so it adds nothing. Depending on the engine, comparing a date to a string could raise a type error instead of simply returning true.
passes_when: status is "ACTIVE" and activated_on is not null (and not equal to the empty string "")
status is anything other than "ACTIVE" (e.g. "INACTIVE", "PENDING", other text), regardless of activated_on, including when activated_on is null
status is null: the comparison to "ACTIVE" is false, so the rule passes (this assumes null compares as not equal rather than raising an error)
